::: {.statx-chapter-banner}
## From one sample to a defensible conclusion

This lab will use repeated sampling to show why estimates vary and how uncertainty shapes statistical decisions.
:::

## Learning objectives

By the end of this lab, students will be able to:

1. Generate and interpret a sampling distribution.
2. Explain the Central Limit Theorem through simulation.
3. Construct and interpret a confidence interval.
4. Connect hypotheses, p-values, errors, power, and sample size.

## Planned workflow

::: {.statx-topic-grid}
::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 1. Repeated samples

Draw many samples from a known population and track the behavior of their means.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 2. Confidence intervals

Visualize interval coverage and identify the meaning of the confidence level.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 3. Hypothesis testing

Translate a research question into hypotheses and interpret evidence without binary thinking.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 4. Power lab

Change effect size, variability, and sample size to see when a study can detect a real effect.
:::
:::

## Deliverables

- A sampling-distribution visualization
- A confidence-interval interpretation
- A complete hypothesis-test conclusion
- A short power and sample-size reflection
